 Judgment
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That, on 16.12.2023 at about 10.25 a.m. the petitioner was proceeding in motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-06-HF-7986 on the left side of the Nagarabhavi Service Road, Opp. to House No.543, Sri Sari Nivasa, Bengaluru, at that time, driver of Bolero Jeep bearing registration No.KA-57-F-530 came at high speed from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
As a result of which, the petitioner thrown on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to G.M.Nursing Home, after first aid treatment, he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent huge amount towards medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.
4.

It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and aged about 23 years, working at driver and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month and he used to spend the said amount for the maintenance of his family members.
After the accident, he could not do any work due to accidental injuries.
5. It is contended that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the Bolero Jeep bearing registration No.KA-57-F-530.
In this regard, case was registered against driver of said vehicle by the jurisdictional Kamakshipalya Traffic Police in Crime No.368/2023.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition seeking compensation.
6. After registration of the case, notices were issued to the respondents.
The respondent No.1 & 2 have appeared before this court through their respective counsel and filed their written statements.
7. In the written statement, the respondent No.1 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further, admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of BMTC Jeep bearing registration No.KA-57 F-530 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and Suresha vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19128695/
2 conditions of the policy.

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note here that petitioner himself has been charge sheeted as A1 for the offence, by jurisdictional police after detailed investigation and obtaining CCTV footages from the place of accident.

It is also contention of the respondent that the petitioner riding the motor cycle under the influence of alcohol and he has been booked under Sec. 185 of MV Act drunk and drive by the police notice No. W/33/15098/875 dated 16.12.2023 and the accident has taken place only due to the place only due to the negligence of the petitioner and he himself is the tortfeasor, this respondent is insurer of BMTC Jeep is not a necessary party to the petition and is not liable to pay any compensation.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
Ultimately, stated that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exaggerated and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.
8. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 has stated that Bolero Jeep bearing No.KA-57-F-0530 was insured with 1st respondent.
Further contended that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the Bolero Jeep.
On the contrary the petitioner was responsible for the alleged accident.

Further stated that at the time of accident the BMTC Jeep was having qualified person to drive the driving vehicle and the rider of the motor cycle was not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
Ultimately contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

9. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident which is the result of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Bolero Jeep bearing registration No.KA- 57-F-530 ?
2. Whether the respondent No.1 proves that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself?
3.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, at what rate and from whom?
4. What order or award?
10. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, petitioner has placed his affidavit evidence in lieu of examination-in-chief, who examined as PW1 and got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.

In addition to his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.Chidananda K.J.C. as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P11 to Ex.P13.
11.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has examined it official as RW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R4 to Ex.R16.
During the course of cross-examination of PW1 the learned counsel for respondent No.1 confronted document at Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioner has filed the written arguments and heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and perused the materials available on record.

13. My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Negative  Issue No.2: In the Affirmative  Issue No.3: Does not arise for  consideration  Issue No.4: As per final order,
 for the following:
 R E A S O N S  ISSUE No.1 & 2:-
14.

These issues are interlinked with each other in order to avoid repetition of facts these issues are taken together for common discussion.
15.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Bolero Jeep bearing registration No.KA-57-F-530 the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.

16. On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has contended in its written statement that, admittedly the petitioner was riding the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-06-HF-7986 in a rash and negligent manner, under the influence of alcohol and unable to control the vehicle while overtaking vehicles hit the Bolero Jeep bering No.KA-57-F-530 coming in the right track from the opposite direction of the road, resulting in the alleged accident.

Further contended that the petitioner himself has been charge sheeted as A1 for the offence and sketch clearly indicates that the petitioner has come to the opposite track where the jeep was being driver by its driver on the right track and has hit the right side portion of the Jeep himself.
The spot mahazar also indicates that, the accident occurred on the extreme right side of the opposite track.
17. Hence, it is necessary to discuss the evidence available on record in order to come to the proper conclusion whether the petitioner is a successful to prove the above issues.
18. The petitioner in order to prove his case, examined as PW1.
In his examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
PW1 in support of his oral evidence has relied upon Ex.P1 to Ex.P5 and Ex.P10.
Ex. P1-true copy of FIR, Ex.P2-true copy of complaint given by the petitioner, Ex.P3-spot mahazar conducted on 16.12.2023, Ex.P4-IMV report and Ex.P5 & 10 are the wound certificates.

19. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by the petitioner, the S.H.O. of Kamakshipalya Trffic police has registered the case against the driver of the Bolero Jeep for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 338 of I.P.C.

4 20.

sentences.text: In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.1 examined official, Legal Department of the respondent No.1 company as RW1.

He has placed the documents i.e.,authorisation letter, spot mahazar, charge sheet, spot sketch, accident, complaint, 65B certificate, statement of witnesses,
police notice, and policy copy as per Ex.R1 to Ex.R16.
He has reiterated the averments made in the written statement.
21. In order to find out the truth in connection with the rival contentions of both the parties proper documentary evidence is required herein.

22. On going through the complaint marked at Ex.P2 given by petitioner, primafacie reveals that,
case was registered agaisnt driver of the Bolero jeep.
On going through the mahazar marked at Ex.P3 & Ex.R5 reveal that, both the vehicles i.e., motor cycle and Bolero jeep seized at the time of mahazar process.

Ex.P4- IMV report shows that BMTC jeep front right side bumper, head light and fender damaged, front right side wind shield glass damaged and motor cycle front forks bent, head light assembly damaged, front right side crash guard bent and front both side indicators damaged.

Further Ex.R7-spot sketch speaks that Jeep was coming its corrrect side, the rider of motor bike came its extreme right side from opposite direction, accident spot shown in the said sketch and other circumstances found in the statement of the witnesses at Ex.R10 to Ex.R14, goes to show that,
due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle, alleged accident had taken place.
23. Further on perusal of Ex.R1 to Ex.R3 photographs clearly shows that the petitioner was coming extremely on its right side and dashed against the jeep.
The petitioner has clearly identified the said photograps in his cross-examination.
24. Surprisingly, the petitioner has not placed charge sheet.
RW1 has placed charge sheet at Ex.R6.

On going through the final report submitted by the investigation officer, after due investigation process, had filed charge sheet against Suresh i.e. petitioner, alleging that, he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC and Section 185 of IMV Act.
It is crystal clear from the investigation papers that, the petitioner himself was the tortfeasor in connection with the alleged accident.
Though the first information was registered against the name of the driver of the Jeep, ultimately charge sheet speaks that, the petitioner himself was responsible for the accident.
The said charghesheet has not been questioned by the petitioner well in time, to prove his innocence.

25. At the time of the argument, learned counsel for the petitioner argued that, the police papers are not the substantive piece of documents, the claims tribunal are duty bound to determine compensation on admitted facts and strict rules of Evidence Act need not be applied in a case of motor vehicle accident and relied the decision of Mallamma V/s. Balaji and others in ILR 2003 Kar 493.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka laid down principle that "strict rules of Evidence Act need not be applied in a case of motor vehicle accident to prove rash and negligent driving."

5 26.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent company, highlighted the point that,
when the petitioner himself being the tortfeasor, question of considering his case for grant of compensation does not arise.

And also argued that, the petition filed under section 166 of M.V Act,
will not come under the purview of the present facts and circumstances of the case.
27. In support of the evidence of the petitioner, no substantive documents placed on record, to impeach the recitals of the final report submitted by the investigation officer.
Though the police papers are not substantive piece of evidence, in the absence of the contra materials, it can be believed.

Apart from this, to prove the stand of the petitioner, has not made an effort to examine any eye witness, to bringforth the truth before the court and also the petitioner has not seriously disputed the damages mentioned in the report of the motor vehicle inspector.

28. On the other hand, at the time of the cross- examination of RW2, except few suggestions,
learned counsel for the petitioner has not made an effort to elicit the point in connection with the innocence of the petitioner and negligence on the part of the driver of the Bolero Jeep.

When the petitioner is taking strong contention about the negligence on the part of the driver of the Bolero Jeep, then duty is more on his part to bringforth cogent and convincing evidence to prove the same to the satisfaction of the court.
In the column No.17 of the charge sheet, there is a clear narration that, as on the date of the accident, the petitioner was negligently riding his motor cycle by consuming alcohol.
Consequently, accident had taken place.

After filing charge sheet against the petitioner by setting aside the recitals of the first information about the allegation against the driver of the BMTC Jeep, he has not questioned the final report, to prove his innocence.
In the absence of the material documents or evidence, the petitioner herein, alleging against the driver of the BMTC Jeep.

29. At the time of cross-examination of the PW1, denied the suggestion that, final report has been filed against him and pleaded his ignorance to the suggestion that he was under the influence of alcohol, as on the date of the accident.

Over all appreciation of the answers given by the PW1, it is crystal clear that, to impeach the charge sheet filed against him, no cogent and convincing evidence available on record for consideration.
As per the charge sheet, the petitioner himself is tortfeasor for commission of accident.

30. At this juncture the counsel for the respondent No.1 has relied the following decisions;
 1) MFA No.4401/2007 in between Venkataramanaiah Guntapadi V/s. M/s. Sparrow Electronics Ltd., and another 2) MFA No.21104/2013 (MV) in between Sanjeev Vs. Shri Balaji Transport Lines (Regd.) & Another

entities.text: Venkataramanaiah Guntapadi V/s. M/s. Sparrow Electronics Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sanjeev Vs. Shri Balaji Transport Lines (Regd.) & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein

the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that, "the claim petition filed u/s 166 of the M.V.
Act 1988 requires the factum of actionable negligence to be proved to seek the compensation.
If the driver himself proves to be negligent, he is not entitled to claim the compensation as the victim of the accident; tort feasor cannot be the claimant."

Suresha vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19128695/
6 31.

entities.text: Suresha vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case also, the petitioner himself is the tortfasor, cannot claim compensation u/s 166 of the M.V. Act.
Hence, the decision relied by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 is aptly applicable to the facts of this case.
32. Now, it is also relevant to note that, when the charge sheet has been submitted against petitioner, then petitioner cannot file the petition under section 166 of M.V. Act.
The Motor Vehicle Act, speaks that, offender can be held liable in the case of an accident, so that, the compensation can be provided to those who suffered because of fault of others.
This Act aims at preventing road accident as well as serve as a legislative mechanism in case of unfortunate accident occurs.

Where death or permanent disablement of any person has resulted from an accident arising out of the use of Motor Vehicle or Motor Vehicles, the owner of the vehicle shall or as the case may be the owner of the vehicle jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

33. In the case on hand, no satisfactory evidence available on record to prove the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the BMTC Jeep bearing registration No. KA-57-F-530, on the fateful day of the accident.

In such a situation, one cannot come to the conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved the actionable negligence on the part of the vehicle against whom the petitioner is making allegation.
As such, the petitioner has utterly failed to place satisfactory evidence by complying all the ingredients of Section 166 of the M.V. Act.
In the light of the discussion held above and in the light of the above said decision, I am answering the issue No.1 and issue No.2 is in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
34.
In the light of the discussion on the issue No.1 & 2, question of answering the issue No.3 does not arise.

ISSUE No.4:
31.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is hereby dismissed.
No order as to costs.
Draw award accordingly.
